subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up — deployment mode decision & GPU recommendations
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@northwindretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & deployment mode

Marissa / team — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can lock internal approvals: 

Summary of our needs:
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity (we need predictable throughput and data isolation; on-prem is a future check but not required today)
- Workload profile: mix of generation + embeddings for search/ranking. Rough mix: ~80% text generation, ~20% embedding requests.
- Traffic targets: peak ~150 requests/sec (RPS) for generation flows; average ~60 RPS. Concurrency target (user-facing): ~40 concurrent live requests at peak.
- Token mix: generation average ~256 tokens per request, ~5% of requests long-form (~2k tokens). Embeddings average 512 tokens per batch.
- Latency SLO: 95th < 600ms for single-turn generation (we realize this depends on model choice).

Questions we need answered to finalize sizing and procurement: 
1) GPU recommendation: H100 vs A100 (we're evaluating cost vs perf). Which gives better throughput for the family of models we discussed (opt-6.7B / 13B and a tuned 70B candidate)?
2) Rough node count / pool sizing to meet the targets above (including headroom for spikes).
3) Support for burst/overflow to hosted API during extreme spikes.

Appreciate any initial numbers — we need something to present to procurement by end of next week.

Best,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of AI Platform, Northwind Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@northwindretail.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & deployment mode

Thanks Samir — great to meet yesterday. I captured your summary below and opened a small workbook with our initial assumptions so we can iterate. Attachment: redwood_dedicated_capacity_workbook.xlsx (worksheet: Northwind_Retail_Sizing).

Couple of quick clarifications before Rafael provides sizing guidance: 
- When you say 150 RPS peak, is that 150 generation requests/sec (i.e., excluding embeddings) or total API calls?
- For the long-form 2k-token tail (~5%), are those synchronous user-facing requests or asynchronous batch jobs? (affects latency headroom and batching).

Next steps I propose:
1) Rafael — can you add a short recommended config (GPU type + node count) to the workbook based on the assumptions below?
2) Samir — if you can confirm the two clarifications above today, we’ll turn around a formal capacity estimate and a recommended Dedicated pool setup by Thurs 13 Aug.
3) I’ll also include recommended fallback policy to Redwood Hosted for bursts, and note contract/SLAs for Dedicated.

Assumptions in the workbook: 
- Model family: opt-13B for most gen, a tuned 70B for a small % of requests (~10% of gen).
- Avg token generation: 256 tokens; 5% at 2k tokens (synchronous).
- Embeddings: small %, can be batched (avg 512 tokens per batch).

Thanks — cc'ing Rafael for the sizing.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@northwindretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & deployment mode

Hi Samir / Marissa — quick sizing notes after reviewing the call recording and the workbook (attached: capacity_estimate_20260812.pdf). High level recommendation based on the workload you described: 

Recommendation summary:
- Deployment: Dedicated pool with Hosted overflow (burst) enabled. Keeps predictable baseline while allowing elastic spikes to Hosted API.
- GPU type: H100 (80GB variant) preferred for 70B-class workloads and mixed sequence lengths; A100 (80GB) is reasonable for opt-13B-only setups and has a cost advantage if you can avoid 70B traffic.
- Baseline pool sizing (to hit ~150 RPS peak for generation with headroom): 
  - If 10% of gen requests hit 70B: Recommend 4 nodes with 4x H100 (16 H100 GPUs total) — this configuration gives you ~180-220 gen RPS (256-token avg) with 95th latency often < 600ms under steady-state.
  - If you restrict to 13B models only: 8x A100 (80GB) spread across 2-4 nodes (depending on instance flavor) should meet the same RPS with ~20-30% lower infra cost.

Concurrency / batching notes:
- Target concurrency: design for 40-60 concurrent active sessions; continuous batching and KV cache will reduce per-token compute.
- Token mix impact: the 5% 2k-token tail increases average token/sec by ~15% — factor that into cost/headroom.

Operational notes and next steps:
- We’ll size the Dedicated pool as above and provide an estimated monthly cost delta between H100 and A100 options in the workbook.
- Suggested rollout: start with H100-heavy pool if you expect >10% 70B usage, otherwise go A100-focused to reduce spend.
- We can configure automatic overflow to Hosted API for short spikes; include burst budget and throttling policy in the mutual action plan.

I attached a short PDF with the assumptions and a table of expected RPS per GPU for our tuned kernels. Happy to walk through with your infra team — available Thurs 13 Aug 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 14 Aug 09:00-12:00 PT.

Rgds,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir@northwindretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity sizing & deployment mode

Thanks — that helps a lot, Rafael. Confirming: the 150 RPS is generation-only (embeddings separate) and the 2k-token tail is synchronous (user-facing).

Let’s take the Thurs 13 Aug slot you mentioned (I realize the date is earlier — can we instead do Fri 14 Aug 10:30 PT?). Priya and I will join. Also can you include SOC 2 and contract/term docs in the follow-up? Procurement will want those with the sizing worksheet.

Appreciate it — speak soon.
Samir
